title: PDIP: Priority Directed Instruction Prefetching
problem: Modern server workloads with large code footprints experience front-end bottlenecks from instruction cache misses. Even with aggressive FDIP (Fetch Directed Instruction Prefetching) in modern processors, significant front-end stalls persist from I-Cache misses that FDIP cannot fully hide.
motivation: Instruction cache misses are a critical bottleneck limiting performance in server workloads with large code footprints.
method: PDIP identifies which I-Cache misses actually impact front-end performance versus those tolerated by FDIP mechanisms. It applies priority-directed prefetching to target only misses that cause stalls, coordinating with existing FDIP to avoid redundant prefetch effort on misses already hidden by the processor.
key_novelty: Instruction prefetching should target only misses causing performance impact rather than reducing all I-Cache misses, requiring coordination with FDIP mechanisms.
contributions: Characterization of which I-Cache misses impact front-end performance versus those hidden by FDIP
Priority-directed prefetching mechanism coordinated with FDIP processors
Performance improvement for server workloads by focusing prefetch efforts on impactful misses
